messages:
kevin: Quick Q — I had to pay an expedited visa fee (personal card) and separately bought one-week travel insurance for a client visit. Can both be reimbursed? company card couldn't be used for the visa charge.

maya (People Ops): Short answer: maybe. Policy details: visa fees required for business travel/relocation are reimbursable with receipts. Expedited processing can be reimbursed but we need manager preapproval or a documented urgent business reason. Travel insurance is not routinely reimbursed unless the trip is high-risk or the customer/contract requires it.

olivia (Finance): To process any of this we need itemized receipts showing vendor name, line-item description (e.g., "visa fee", "expedited service", "policy premium"), policy/coverage dates, and the currency. If you used a personal card, attach the card/bank statement line as well. Also include manager approval note.

kevin: I didn't get written preapproval for the expedited fee — manager verbally okayed it because it was same-day. Is that acceptable?

maya (People Ops): Verbal is okay if you can capture it in writing after the fact. Upload the manager's Slack thread or an email saying they approved the expedited fee, include approver name, timestamp, and short rationale. Retro approvals are accepted but will trigger a manual review.

kevin: The insurance was purchased as part of a bundle on the travel site and the PDF has only one total line.

olivia (Finance): In that case request an itemized invoice from the vendor showing separate charge lines. If vendor cannot provide itemization, submit the PDF and add a note explaining the bundle. Finance will manually verify — that may slow reimbursement.

kevin: Do I need to convert currencies myself?

olivia (Finance): Submit receipts in original currency. Our expense system converts using the transaction date rate for bookkeeping. You can add your own conversion note, but we will use the tool's rate.

kevin: What about spouse/companion fees — they joined for a couple extra days and incurred visa/insurance charges.

maya (People Ops): Companion/spouse costs are personal and not covered unless explicitly approved beforehand (rare). Exceptions: when partner attendance is required by the customer or travel policy was explicitly extended to include dependents — that must be documented in advance.

kevin: Understood, thanks. Any quick checklist I should follow when I upload?

maya (People Ops): Yes — include: 1) itemized receipt or vendor invoice, 2) manager approval (pre or retro), 3) bank/card statement line if paid personally, 4) brief justification in expense notes, 5) policy name/coverage dates for insurance.

olivia (Finance): Example note you can paste into the expense report:

```
Trip: NYC client visit (project-XYZ)
Expense: Expedited visa fee
Amount: EUR 180
Paid with: personal card (last 4 digits: 1234)
Manager approval: @sarah (sent 2025-11-12 09:14)
Justification: same-day embassy appointment required for travel on 2025-11-14
```

kevin: Perfect — I'll request the itemized invoice and upload everything.

expense-bot: Reminder: upload receipts and attach approvals in the Expenses app. Missing documentation will delay payout.

maya (People Ops): TL;DR — visa fees reimbursable when required + receipts; expedited needs approval (retro allowed with proof); travel insurance reimbursed only if approved/required; spouse costs not covered without preapproval; always try to get itemized invoices. :white_check_mark: 

olivia (Finance): If you want, tag me when you've uploaded and I'll kick off a manual review so it doesn't sit in the queue. :wave:
